doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Booking at the North Park Hotel, then Rush Street
summary: He explains how off-night shows grew into weekend bookings of Yusef Lateef, Elvin Jones and Rahsaan Roland Kirk, then moves to Wells and Rush streets.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So how did you go about then identifying, booking these bands? Cause we’re...

Well, it first started as off-night stuff. And before I started booking five nights a week on Russ Street, I had a place called the North Park Hotel, which is up near Grant Park. I was doing Sunday afternoons and evenings, and they were well attended, and it was all ages. It sat a couple hundred, maybe five hundred in the ballroom. I contacted Yusef, cause I had known him from Chicago, and he said, “well I can’t really” - he was

in Detroit then - “I can’t really come down for one night.” I said, “well...” so we tried Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and it worked. And then I booked Elvin; I booked Rahsaan Roland Kirk, and became a sensation here. Then we had a chance to move. Let’s see, we had a place on Wells Street called the Brown Shoe, which was a huge place. It used to be a restaurant called Paul Bunyan. We then moved to the basement of the Happy Medium at Rush and Delaware, and of course Russ Street was a big entertainment center then. Wanna take a break?
